reason:
The number is right and the diagnosis is wrong, and the diagnosis is the whole finding. I reproduced the measurement exactly: documentElement.scrollHeight - clientHeight is 107 at 1024x800, 1152x800, 1279x800, 1280x900, 1440x800, 1440x960 and 1920x1080, in owner-flight, owner-editing, owner-undone and owner-draft alike. 107 is not a mystery and it is not the product: it is 40px of --stage-pad above + 15px of .tl-caption + 12px gap = a 67px offset, plus 40px of --stage-pad below. shell.css names both of those in its own comments - --stage-pad exists so 'one page can show a phone artifact, a desk artifact and an A4 sheet honestly', and of .tl-caption it says in as many words 'It is lab furniture, not product'. The finding measures the lab's picture frame and reports the painting as crooked. Mounted at the document root, which is what the round note is a claim about, 100dvh is exact and the range is 0.

The finding's actual charge - 'this is the same defect the file records as fixed, a smaller number wearing a new mechanism' and 'a fix recorded as done that the composition around it makes inert' - is measurably false, and I drove it rather than reasoned about it. The round-8 defect was uncommanded movement: the document height CHANGED when the editor opened and closed, so the browser clamped the view out from under a delete. At 1440x960, scrolled deliberately to the bottom (scrollY 107) and then driven all the way through - open the editor, four stepper presses, Delete, Undo - scrollHeight stays 1067, range stays 107, scrollY stays 107 and .b-ownerField's height stays 960 at every single step. The height is constant with the editor open and closed and through a delete and its undo; nothing repaints the horizon, nothing clamps, nothing moves under the hand. The frame is doing exactly what the comment says it does, and the panes scroll their own content (.b-plan 664px client over 1727px of plan at 1440x960). Calling it inert is the one thing the evidence will not support.

What the finding offers as harm - 'scrolling it moves .b-num from y=268 to y=161' - is the reviewer choosing to scroll 107px of stage margin. That is not the horizon travelling; that is the lab's mat sliding. 'Scrolling the window to follow a move at desk width' is settled twice over precisely because the window must not move on its own, and it does not.

The fix also overreaches its own gate line. It proposes asserting scrollHeight - clientHeight === 0 'for the owner states', but owner-empty is [data-medium="full"] with no .b-ownerField for the :has() to catch, and it measures 37 at every 800-tall viewport. The assertion as worded fails on its own patch.

Refuted: overstated commit message about lab chrome, not a defect in the artifact.
sharpenedFix: One measured residue is worth carrying forward, and it is not what this finding argued. Because the 100dvh frame starts 67px down, its last line falls past the window edge: at EVERY desk size tested (1024x800, 1152x800, 1279x800, 1280x900, 1440x800, 1440x960, 1920x1080) the .b-foot provenance line - 'Kept by Orla · Updated 15 July 2026 · Signal Timeline' - has a text box of top = innerHeight-4, bottom = innerHeight+11, so roughly 4px of a 15px line is above the fold and the glyphs are all but gone. shots.mjs screenshots the viewport, not the full page, so every shipped desk frame the panel grades shows the closing rule with a shaved sliver of type under it. If a later round wants that, it is a one-line lab-stage change scoped to the owner's desk states - drop --stage-pad's bottom half and the offset for [data-medium="full"] .tl-page:has(.b-ownerField) so the 100dvh frame is the viewport - and it should be argued as 'the graded frames clip the product's own foot', not as 'the page still scrolls'. Do not ship the assertion as written; if one is added it must exclude owner-empty, which has no .b-ownerField and measures 37 at 800 tall.
